class_guess: two-zone block/pair shuffler (chaotic two-stack list machine), not a counter
summary: Blocks left of the head, pairs right of it; exact macro rules; halting needs an even zero run; parity holds, proof open.
mechanism: Two zones split at the head: left = 1-blocks split by single 0s, right = (10)-pairs split by zero runs (plus a rare lone 1). A/F sweeps left turn a block into pairs; B/C passes right turn pairs into blocks. E-event K(L; a; r; R) = `L 1^a E> 0^r R`.

Exact rules (12,000/12,000 random, all 34.5M E-events from blank to 1e9): even a -> Ee eats the last two closed blocks y, b: `K(L; y+3; b+1; (10)^(a/2) 0^(r-2) R)`. Odd a -> Eo closes a block 2, then a C-pass turns pairs into blocks until a run 0^n, n >= 3 (`a = x+2, r = n-2`) or a lone 1 (`a = y+3, r = x+1`). The block list is shuffled chaotically.

Halting needs a C-pass to meet exactly 0^2. Closed blocks stay even and zero runs odd (1.7M E-events to 5e7), and every rule keeps this, but only under side conditions (no lone pair before a run; a = 2 only at the edge) that are not yet shown inductive.

history.skeleton: right-edge E-events (r = inf, R empty): 0^inf 1^b1 0 1^b2 0 ... 0 1^bp 0 1^a E> 0^inf

rules.name: Ee (even head block, a = 2k)
rules.cases: k >= 1, r >= 3. r = 1: tail (10)^(k-1) 1 R (creates a lone 1). r = inf: tail (10)^k 0^inf. Missing y, b count as 0 (left edge: a' = 3, r' = 1, tape grows left by 1).

rules.name: C1-C2 (C-pass over pairs)
rules.cases: C2 closes the block x+2 at a single 0; needs j >= 1 after it (always so).

rules.name: C3 (C-pass meets 0^n, n >= 3 or inf)
rules.cases: n = 3 gives r = 1; n = inf is the right edge (right record, +4 cells).

rules.name: C4 (C-pass meets a lone 1)
rules.cases: A zero run at the front of (10)^(j-1) Q merges into r. A missing y counts as 0.

rules.name: H (halting pattern)
rules.to: halt: C, D write 1, E reads 1
rules.cases: The only way E reads 1. It needs an even zero run of length 2 after a pair, which INV excludes.

template.diff: 1 transition: our A0 = 1RB, template (in our names) A0 = 1LC; v2-v4 have 0LB there (v4 also E0 = 1LD)
template.note: All four proved neighbours differ exactly at A0, the turn that starts rule Ee. v1 is a deterministic counter on a fixed skeleton (SkelE n, Bnext on (n, j, b), ClosedCall, GoodB). Here the block list is a shuffled stack, so only the top-level shape (progress_nonhalt_cond + an invariant) carries over.

strategy: Find an inductive invariant over the validated macro model: closed blocks even, runs odd, plus local context conditions. Search it mechanically (regular/bigram closure over abstract tokens, or a TM-level CTL certificate). Then write rules Ee/Eo/C1-C4 as es/ind lemmas and close with progress_nonhalt_cond; one proof would cover 469 and 599 (start D).
risks: The context conditions may not be local: simple versions fail random closure (~2% of steps), and 'r = 1 implies next group >= 3 pairs' fails on the real run at step 2,403,364.
Chaotic list dynamics: if no small invariant closes, a CTL certificate may be large; 85 small RWL_mod/NG settings returned false.
No template help: the proved neighbours differ exactly in the slot that drives rule Ee.
